record.context_brief: Automorphisms of antilattices and their congruence lattices
record.original_question: For an antilattice N, each automorphism alpha of N induces an automorphism alpha-hat of its congruence lattice Con(N), yielding a group homomorphism h: Aut N -> Aut Con(N). Classify exactly those antilattices N for which this homomorphism h is an isomorphism.

evidence.quote: Any automorphism α of N induces an automorphism α̂ of Con(N ).
Classify those antilattices N for which h is an isomorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An antilattice is an algebraic structure $(N,\wedge,\vee)$ consisting of a nonempty set $N$ equipped with two binary operations $\wedge$ and $\vee$ such that each of $(N,\wedge)$ and $(N,\vee)$ is a semigroup (in fact a band: idempotent semigroup), and such that the two operations are mutually anti-absorbing, i.e. for all $x,y\in N$,
\[ x\wedge y = x\vee y \;\Longrightarrow\; x=y. \]
A congruence on $N$ is an equivalence relation $\theta$ on $N$ that is compatible with both operations; the set $\operatorname{Con}(N)$ of all congruences on $N$, ordered by inclusion, forms a complete lattice. Let $\operatorname{Aut}(N)$ denote the group of automorphisms of $N$ and $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Con}(N))$ the group of automorphisms of its congruence lattice. Each automorphism $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(N)$ induces an automorphism $\hat\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Con}(N))$ by $\hat\alpha(\theta)=\{(\alpha(x),\alpha(y)):(x,y)\in\theta\}$, and the assignment $\alpha\mapsto\hat\alpha$ defines a group homomorphism
\[ h:\operatorname{Aut}(N)\to\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Con}(N)). \]
Classify, up to isomorphism, exactly those antilattices $N$ for which the homomorphism $h$ is an isomorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published classification resolving when the induced map from the automorphism group of an antilattice to the automorphism group of its congruence lattice is an isomorphism. While related results on independence of automorphism groups and congruence lattices for ordinary lattices are well known, no specific resolution of this antilattice problem was found.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Independence Theorem for Automorphism Groups and Congruence Lattices of Arbitrary Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Strong independence results for automorphism groups and congruence lattices of lattices.
status_evidence.claim: Related independence results exist for ordinary lattices, but they do not address the antilattice classification asked here.
